glossary.definition: A vehicle or engineered system designed to operate in space. A satellite is one type of spacecraft.
The rocket that carries a spacecraft from Earth toward its deployment orbit.
An object orbiting another body. In this guide it means an artificial spacecraft orbiting Earth.
A small satellite built around standardized unit sizes and dispenser interfaces.
One CubeSat unit, approximately a 10 cm cube under the current CubeSat design specification; larger formats combine units.
A CubeSat roughly three units long, providing more volume than a 1U spacecraft.
The supporting platform—power, computing, communications, structure, thermal and attitude control—that enables the payload.
The instrument or experiment that performs the mission's main purpose.
The complete objective and lifecycle of the spacecraft, including design, testing, launch and operations.
An orbit relatively close to Earth, commonly used by CubeSats.
Height above a reference Earth surface.
The curved path followed by a spacecraft under gravity.
Time required to complete one orbit.
Angle between the orbital plane and Earth's equatorial plane.
The geometric plane containing the spacecraft's idealized orbit.
Time-tagged information describing where a celestial body or spacecraft is expected to be.
A force/effect that makes a real orbit differ from an ideal two-body orbit.
Interval when Earth or another body blocks direct sunlight from the spacecraft.
Direction from the spacecraft/reference frame toward the Sun.
Orientation of a spacecraft in space; it is different from altitude.
Coordinate system used to describe position, velocity or attitude.
Earth-based equipment that communicates with the spacecraft.
Period when the spacecraft is visible to a ground station and communication may be possible.
Measurements and status data transmitted from the spacecraft.
Instruction transmitted from the ground to the spacecraft.
Subsystem responsible for electrical generation, storage, control and distribution.
Power Management and Distribution; circuits that condition, control and deliver electrical power.
On-Board Computer; runs flight software and coordinates spacecraft functions.
Command and Data Handling; receives commands, handles data and supports onboard processing/storage.
Attitude Determination and Control System; estimates and controls orientation.
Telemetry, Tracking and Command; communication functions used to monitor and operate the spacecraft.
Methods used to keep spacecraft components within required temperature ranges.
Motor-driven wheel that changes spacecraft attitude through angular momentum exchange.
Electromagnetic actuator that interacts with Earth's magnetic field to create control torque.
Predefined low-risk state that protects essential functions after a serious anomaly or low-energy condition.
Extra hardware, software or paths intended to tolerate a failure.
Fault Detection, Isolation and Recovery; identify an abnormal condition, locate likely cause and perform/advise a bounded response.
Electrical potential difference that helps drive current.
Rate of electric-charge flow.
Instantaneous rate of energy use or generation; P=VI in a simple DC case.
Power accumulated over time; 10 W for 2 hours is 20 Wh.
Table comparing expected generation and consumption in each mode.
Calculation of generated and consumed energy over a period such as one orbit.
Semiconductor device converting light into electricity.
Connected solar cells/panels that generate spacecraft power.
Angle between incoming sunlight and the solar-panel normal.
Intentionally reducing ideal performance to account for real losses, aging, temperature and uncertainty.
Beginning of Life; performance near the start of the mission.
End of Life; expected performance near mission end after degradation.
Smallest electrochemical unit in a battery.
Connected cells plus protection, structure, sensing and often management electronics.
Lithium-ion rechargeable battery chemistry family widely used where high energy density is valuable.
Battery Management System; electronics/software that monitor and protect a battery within its design limits.
Amount of electric charge a battery can deliver under specified conditions.
Approximate stored electrical energy; depends on voltage and charge capacity.
Estimated percentage of presently available battery charge/energy.
Percentage of capacity removed; approximately 100% minus SOC under the simplified definition.
Estimate of present battery capability relative to a defined new/reference condition.
Estimate of time or cycles before a defined end-of-use criterion; highly dependent on data and assumptions.
Battery voltage measured/estimated without load after suitable rest conditions.
Effective opposition inside the battery that creates voltage drop and heat under current.
Temporary terminal-voltage reduction when load current rises.
Fraction of charging energy stored by the battery in the model.
Fraction accounting for energy lost while delivering power.
Charge/discharge current normalized to battery capacity; 1C nominally corresponds to using rated capacity in about one hour under stated conditions.
Total charged and discharged energy accumulated over time.
Partial cycles combined into the energy equivalent of one full charge-discharge cycle.
Reduction in available battery capacity with aging/use.
Dangerous self-heating condition in which heat-generating reactions accelerate; CubeTwin does not predict or certify this phenomenon.
Mathematical/software representation of selected real-world behaviour.
Running a model over time under defined inputs and assumptions.

A digital representation connected to the state/history of a particular physical system. CubeTwin begins as a physics-based digital-twin simulation; it becomes a calibrated twin only when linked to traceable data from a specific test article or spacecraft.
Simulated time between numerical updates.
Quantity carried from one time step to the next, such as SOC or temperature.
Defined environmental or interface condition used by a model.
Complete set of mission inputs, schedule, faults and duration.
Defined defect or abnormal condition that may cause an undesired effect.
Observed behaviour that differs from expectation; it does not automatically prove the root cause.
Inability to perform a required function within specified limits.
Deliberately adding a simulated fault to test detection and response.
Hidden, authoritative simulated physical state used to assess an observer/detector.
Value that triggers a status, warning or action.
Different entry and exit thresholds used to prevent rapid toggling.
Energy remaining beyond what is required for the planned activity/reserve.
Voltage/power condition too low for correct operation of one or more loads.
Probability or ability to perform required functions for a stated time under stated conditions.
Repeated runs with sampled uncertain inputs to explore a distribution of outcomes.
Starting value that makes pseudo-random simulations reproducible.
Evidence that the software/model was implemented according to its stated requirements—“built correctly.”
Evidence that the model is appropriate for the intended use—“the right model for this purpose.”
Adjusting model parameters using traceable observed/test data.
Quantified lack of exact knowledge about inputs or model behaviour.
Allowed difference between expected and calculated results.
Traceable connection among requirements, parameters, models, tests, data and decisions.
Test setup where real hardware interacts with a simulated environment/system.
Scale used to describe technology maturity; do not assign a TRL without criteria and evidence.
Health and Usage Monitoring System; observes condition and usage to support diagnostics, prognostics and maintenance.

Learn: CubeSat units and the 3U reference mission
Do: form a team of 1–3 active students for ISAST submission
identify users: student team, faculty mentor and mission reviewer
record all example parameters with units and sources/assumption labels
calculate the 500 km circular-orbit period by hand
create the CubeTwin repository branch according to the existing workflow.
Build: first wireframe for desktop and 390 px mobile
landing-page hero and project identity draft.
Verify: dimensional/unit check
hand result versus code within a defined tolerance
invalid altitude inputs return controlled errors
no existing `/space` content or routes regress.

Learn: watt, watt-hour, voltage, current and efficiency
Do: estimate energy required through one eclipse
calculate whether the example battery reserve is sufficient
Build: first SOC-versus-time line chart using a temporary ideal battery.
Verify: solar power is zero during simplified eclipse
net power equals delivered solar minus load
energy-conservation test passes for a one-hour constant-load case
chart labels and tooltips show units.

Learn: capacity, energy, SOC, DoD, charge/discharge efficiency
why temperature and internal resistance matter
Do: create a 3–5 page concept paper or 5–8 slide pitch deck
include problem, solution, novelty, feasibility, impact and references
include active student ID cards as required by the challenge
use screenshots clearly labelled as concept/prototype
complete a submission checklist and retain the submitted PDF.
Build: SOC limits, reserve warning and unmet-load accounting
Verify: SOC cannot exceed configured bounds
charge/discharge losses have correct direction
zero-load and zero-generation edge cases pass
same scenario and seed produce identical output.
Deliverables: submission receipt/reference recorded by the team.

Learn: OCV, terminal voltage and internal resistance
Build: warnings for undervoltage and temperature assumptions
input help, glossary links and validation messages.
Verify: increasing resistance increases voltage sag under equal load
no divide-by-zero, `NaN` or infinite output
thermal model remains stable at allowed time steps
numerical functions have unit tests and explicit units.
Stage Gate 1 acceptance: energy balance closes within defined numerical tolerance
a beginner can run the default scenario without instruction.

Build: schedule editor or preset schedule cards
payload and downlink activity markers on charts
event log with reasons for every mode change.
Verify: the state machine has no unreachable or accidental looping states
safe mode reduces the configured load
recovery requires the higher threshold and dwell time
scheduled activities complete, defer or fail deterministically.

Build: at least six power fault scenarios
fault comparison view: baseline versus faulty run
Verify: each injected fault begins and ends at the configured time
baseline results do not change when no fault is enabled
detectors are tested for expected true/false outcomes
imported scenarios cannot inject code or unsafe markup.

Learn: telemetry, sampling interval and time series
energy throughput and equivalent full cycles
Build: telemetry table and charts for SOC, power, voltage and temperature
JSON/CSV export with units and metadata
accessible chart summaries for screen readers.
Verify: sums/integrals match raw telemetry
exported row count and timestamps are correct
units appear in headers
large 24-hour runs stay within mobile memory limits.

Learn: coordinate frame as a reference for position/orientation
why 3D visuals must not be treated as analysis results
Build: optimized 3D Earth, orbit path, moving CubeSat and day/night indication
quality setting or automatic mobile simplification
static 2D fallback when WebGL is unavailable
Verify: the 3D scene agrees with sunlight/eclipsed state from the numerical engine
no duplicated physics is implemented inside the renderer
touch controls do not block page scrolling
360, 390, 412 and 768 px layouts remain usable
keyboard and screen-reader users can obtain the same numerical information.
Stage Gate 2 acceptance: mission modes, faults, telemetry and 3D view work together
simulation remains responsive on representative mobile hardware
the default scenario can be understood without reading source code.

Learn: deterministic run versus Monte Carlo run
Build: uncertainty inputs for capacity, load, solar output and resistance
seeded batch runner in a worker
probability of falling below reserve and completing activities.
Verify: fixed inputs collapse to the deterministic result
same seed reproduces the same distribution
sample count is capped for mobile safety
claims state simulated probability, not real mission probability.

Learn: test case, expected result and tolerance
Build: tutorial modules, exercises and answer guidance
print stylesheet and printable workbook cover
Verify: orbit-period result is compared to the analytical formula
constant-power battery cases match analytical energy change
energy accounting reports numerical residual
all external sources are authoritative and linked
print preview has no clipped tables, invisible text or unnecessary dark backgrounds.

weeks.title: SEO, AI search and production quality

Build: optional `/llms.txt` summary as a supplemental discovery aid
analytics events for simulator start, scenario completion, workbook print and outbound ecosystem links, without personal data.
Verify: no `noindex` or accidental crawler block
canonical and Open Graph URLs use the exact production path
structured data matches visible content and has no fabricated ratings, partners or awards
page is server-rendered enough for crawlers to understand without running the simulator
broken-link, metadata and sitemap tests pass
Search Console, Bing tools and schema validators are documented as post-deployment checks.

Build: polish the default, low-energy and fault scenarios
complete README, model assumptions, validation report and contributor guide
create a 3–5 minute beginner demonstration script
deploy through the repository's existing verified process.
Verify: full tests, build, lint/type-check and mobile end-to-end tests pass
Lighthouse lab targets are met or documented
no console errors, hydration warnings or broken downloads
simulator output is deterministic when Monte Carlo is off
disclaimers and organization roles are accurate
rollback procedure and known limitations are documented.
Stage Gate 3 / Definition of Done: `/space` contains the new CubeTwin card and no unrelated redesign
educational simulation engine and required scenarios work
equations, units and glossary are understandable to beginners
public claims are accurate and evidence-based
handover material enables a new student to reproduce the demo.
